headlines.title: American Express vs. S&P Global: Which Financial Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
headlines.summary: Two payments and data giants, one a premium card network and the other a gatekeeper of ratings and benchmarks, offer very different paths to growth and risk.

headlines.title: American Express vs. Mastercard: Which Financial Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
headlines.summary: Amex trades at 17.3x forward earnings while Mastercard commands 32.5x, a valuation gap that raises a real question about which payments giant deserves the premium.

headlines.title: Card Networks Like Visa and Mastercard Don't Take Credit Losses. American Express Does. Here's Why That Matters for the Stock.
headlines.summary: The premium card company's stock, owned by Berkshire Hathaway, has outperformed the S&P 500 index in the past five years.

headlines.title: American Express (AXP) Brings AI Payments To Cardholders And Broadens Basketball Perks
headlines.summary: American Express (NYSE:AXP) and OpenAI launched AI-driven payments via ChatGPT Wallet, integrating Amex cards directly into the chat interface. The new ChatGPT Wallet feature allows eligible American Express cardholders to initiate and authorize card payments within ChatGPT conversations. American Express broadened its partnership with the NBA, WNBA, and USA Basketball, adding new global experiential and loyalty perks for cardholders.

headlines.title: Is American Express (AXP) Reasonable After A 104% Run And New Card Deals?
headlines.summary: American Express has delivered strong gains over the past three years, so the real question now is whether the current share price is supported by the returns the business earns on its capital. Over the past 3 years the stock has risen 104.0%, which puts real weight on whether those past returns on capital can justify where the valuation sits today.

description: American Express Company, together with its subsidiaries, operates as an integrated payments company in the United States, Europe, the Middle East and Africa, the Asia Pacific, Australia, New Zealand, Latin America, Canada, the Caribbean, and internationally. It operates through four segments: U.S. Consumer Services, Commercial Services, International Card Services, and Global Merchant and Network Services. The company offers credit and charge cards and complementary products and services, including travel, dining, and lifestyle and expense management products and services; and banking and other payment and financing products and services, including deposits and non-card lending. It also provides merchant acquisition and processing, servicing and settlement, fraud prevention, and point-of-sale marketing and information products and services, as well as network services. The company offers its products and services to consumers, small businesses, mid-sized companies, and large corporations through mobile and online applications, affiliate marketing, customer referral programs, third-party service providers and business partners, in-house sales teams, direct mail, telephone, and direct response advertising. American Express Company was founded in 1850 and is headquartered in New York, New York.
